## 2. CNN

Source: CNN_CIA_Test_1_RegNo_last3digits.ipynb

### Errors

TensorFlow is imported without the alias tf.
The image lacks a batch dimension.
The CNN input shape lacks the channel dimension.
Flatten is missing parentheses and a comma.
The second convolution is selected instead of the first convolution for visualization.

### Corrections

import tensorflow as tf

image = image.reshape(1, 28, 28, 1)

input_shape=(28, 28, 1)

tf.keras.layers.Flatten(),

The model section should contain:

model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(
        filters=32,
        kernel_size=(5, 5),
        activation="sigmoid",
        input_shape=(28, 28, 1)
    ),

    tf.keras.layers.MaxPooling2D(
        pool_size=(3, 3),
        strides=(3, 3)
    ),

    tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(
        filters=8,
        kernel_size=(3, 3),
        activation="sigmoid"
    ),

    tf.keras.layers.MaxPooling2D(
        pool_size=(2, 2)
    ),

    tf.keras.layers.Flatten(),

    tf.keras.layers.Dense(
        32,
        activation="sigmoid"
    )
])

For the first convolution feature map:

feature_model = tf.keras.Model(
    inputs=model.input,
    outputs=model.layers[0].output
)

Expected shapes:

Input shape:                         (1, 28, 28, 1)
Final representation shape:          (1, 32)
First convolution output shape:      (1, 24, 24, 32)

## 3. LeNet-5

Source: LeNet5_CIA_Test_1_RegNo_last3digits.ipynb

### Errors

TensorFlow is imported without the alias tf.
The image is multiplied by 255 even though it already contains values 0 and 255.
The image lacks a batch dimension.
The first pooling layer uses (3, 3), which makes the later 5 × 5 convolution impossible.
Several commas and parentheses are missing.
The output layer has one unit, making argmax meaningless for digit classification.
The feature extractor selects C3 while being named and displayed as C1.

### Corrections

import tensorflow as tf

Normalize correctly:

image = image / 255.0

Add batch and channel dimensions:

image = image.reshape(1, 32, 32, 1)

Use a 2 × 2 pooling window:

x = tf.keras.layers.AveragePooling2D(
    pool_size=(2, 2),
    name="S2"
)(x)

Correct model code:

inputs = tf.keras.Input(shape=(32, 32, 1))

x = tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(
    6, kernel_size=(5, 5),
    activation="relu",
    name="C1"
)(inputs)

x = tf.keras.layers.AveragePooling2D(
    pool_size=(2, 2),
    name="S2"
)(x)

x = tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(
    8,
    kernel_size=(3, 3),
    activation="tanh",
    name="C3"
)(x)

x = tf.keras.layers.AveragePooling2D(
    pool_size=(2, 2),
    name="S4"
)(x)

x = tf.keras.layers.Conv2D(
    120,
    kernel_size=(5, 5),
    activation="tanh",
    name="C5"
)(x)

x = tf.keras.layers.Flatten(name="Flatten")(x)

features = tf.keras.layers.Dense(
    84,
    activation="tanh",
    name="F6"
)(x)

outputs = tf.keras.layers.Dense(
    10,
    activation="softmax",
    name="Output"
)(features)

model = tf.keras.Model(inputs=inputs, outputs=outputs)

Correct feature extraction:

c1_model = tf.keras.Model(
    inputs=model.input,
    outputs=model.get_layer("C1").output
)

Expected shapes:

CNN input shape:       (1, 32, 32, 1)
Output shape:          (1, 10)
C1 feature map shape:  (1, 28, 28, 6)
